text_string: Signa uero humilitatis sunt humilitas habitus, uultus et gestus, abiectio sui, uehementia seipsum accusandi.
trad_string: The signs of humility are humility in garment, in expression, and in gesture; self-abasement; and a strong eagerness to accuse oneself.

source_label: Petrus Cantor Parisiensis, Verbum adbreviatum (textus conflatus)
text_string: Dictum est quod inuidie mater est superbia, detractionis inuidia, et ita detractio est pessima neptis superbie. Contra istas tres pessimas pestes militat humilitas quasi per antithesim contra toxicum illarum antidotum.
trad_string: It has been said that the mother of envy is pride, that envy gives birth to detraction, and thus detraction is the most wicked granddaughter of pride. Against these three most grievous plagues, humility fights as if by antithesis, an antidote to their poison.

source_label: Alanus ab Insulis, De virtutibus et de vitiis et de doni spiritus sancti
text_string: Humilitas est uirtus per quam animus in nullo se efferens, nichilque bonum sibi ascribens, exterius etiam deiecti prefert habitum. Humilitas autem diuiditur in tres species: in illam qua homo se humiliat maiori, que dicitur sufficiens; et in illam qua homo se humiliat pari, que dicitur perfecta; et in illam qua se humiliat minori, que dicitur superabundans.
trad_string: Humility is the virtue by which the soul, exalting itself in nothing and attributing no good to itself, even outwardly prefers the appearance of lowliness. Humility, moreover, is divided into three kinds: into that by which a person humbles himself before one who is greater, which is called sufficient; and into that by which a person humbles himself before an equal, which is called perfect; and into that by which he humbles himself before one who is lesser, which is called superabundant.

source_label: Conradus Hirsaugiensis, Liber de fructibus carnis et spiritus
text_string: Cognito jam horrendo procinctu superbiae qui trahit ad sinistram, humilitatis exercitum attende qui ducit ad dexteram. Ejus autem hi sunt comitatus principales: Prudentia, justitia, fortitudo, temperantia, fides, spes et charitas.
trad_string: Now that the dreadful battle array of pride, which draws to the left, has been recognized, turn your attention to the army of humility, which leads to the right. Its principal companions, however, are these: prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance, faith, hope, and charity.

source_label: Ps.-Hugo de Sancto Victore, Ps.-Bernardus Claraevallensis, Tractatus de statu virtutum
text_string: Ecce Dei humilitas incomparabilis, quia comparationem dignam non recipit; inaestimabilis, quia aestimari non potest; ineffabilis, quia verbis explicari non potest, ut Deus et Dominus omnium fieret homo et servus omnium, invisibilis videretur, panis Angelorum aleretur, virtus coelorum infirmaretur, vita moreretur; sed huius mysterii causa est, Dei iustitia et misericordia.
trad_string: Behold the incomparable humility of God! In comparable, because it does not admit a worthy com parison; inestimable, because it is not able to be measured; ineffable, because it cannot be explained with words: that the God and Lord of all should be come a man and the servant of all, that the invisible should be seen, that the Lord, the bread of angels would be nourished, that the power of the heavens should be made weak, that life should die. The cause of this mystery is the justice and mercy of God.

source_label: Bernardus Claraevallensis, Liber de gradibus humilitatis et superbiae
text_string: Humilitatis vero talis potest esse definitio: humilitas est virtus, qua homo verissima sui cognitione sibi ipse vilescit.
trad_string: Now this can be the definition of humility: humility is the virtue by which a man, through a most truthful knowledge of himself, becomes lowly in his own eyes.

source_label: Bernardus Claraevallensis, Liber de gradibus humilitatis et superbiae
text_string: Gloriosa res humilitas, qua ipsa quoque superbia palliare se appetit, ne vilescat!
trad_string: Humility is a glorious thing, so glorious that even pride itself seeks to cloak itself with it, lest it become despised.

text_string: Dico ergo primo quod humilitas est voluntaria mentis inclinacio et proprie excellencie contemptus.
trad_string: First, then, I say that humilitas is the voluntary bending of our mind and contempt for our own superiority.

text_string: Nunc autem expleta parte superbie cum suis membris et oblectamentis offert se domina Humilitas econtra tamquam istorum expugnatrix ac bonorum reparatrix. Ipsa enim est radix et fundamentum omnis boni.
trad_string: After the section on pride and its members and false pleasures has been completed, Lady humility now rises against them to overcome them and to restore the good qualities. For she is the root and foundation of every good.

source_label: Humbertus Romanis, Expositio Magistri Humberti super constitutiones fratrum praedicatorum
text_string: Istae sunt tres illae immersiones in flumen humilitatis, quae deorsum tendunt, in quibus immersus fuit Ezechiel, modo usque ad talos, modo usque ad genua, modo usque ad renes, sicut habetur cap. 47 ejusd.
trad_string: These are those three immersions into the river of humility, which descend downward, in which Ezekiel was immersed—up to the ankles, up to the knees, or up to the loins—as is found in chapter 47 of the same book.

text_string: Humilitas uero his indiciis conprobatur: primo si mortificatas in sese omnes habeat uoluntates, secundo si non solum suorum actuum, uerum etiam cogitationum nihil suum celauerit seniorem, tertio si nihil suae discretioni, sed iudicio eius uniuersa committat ac monita eius sitiens ac libenter auscultet, quarto si in omnibus seruet oboedientiae mansuetudinem patientiae que constantiam, quinto si non solum iniuriam inferat nulli, sed ne ab alio quidem sibimet inrogatam doleat atque tristetur, sexto si nihil agat, nihil praesumat, quod non uel communis regula uel maiorum cohortantur exempla, septimo si omni uilitate contentus sit et ad omnia se quae sibi praebentur uelut operarium malum iudicarit indignum, octauo si semet ipsum cunctis inferiorem non superficie pronuntiet labiorum, sed intimo cordis credat affectu, nono si linguam cohibeat uel non sit clamosus in uoce, decimo si non sit facilis ac promptus in risu
trad_string: Humility is proved by these signs: first, if they have their desires mortified in themselves; second, if they do not conceal not only their actions, but also their thoughts from their superior; third, if they commit all things not to their own judgment but to that of their superior, listening eagerly and willingly to his instructions; fourth, if in all things they preserve the mildness of obedience and the perseverance of patience; fifth, if they not only inflict no injury on anyone, but also bear calmly and without sourness any wrong done to them by another; sixth, if they do nothing and dare nothing except what is supported either by the common rule or by the example of their elders; seventh, if they are content with every meanness and judge themselves unworthy of whatever is offered to them, like a bad workman; eighth, if they sincerely believe in their heart, and not only declare with their lips, that they are inferior to all; ninth, if they restrain their tongue and are not loud of voice; tenth, if they are not ready or quick to laugh

text_string: Gestus vero corporis est argumentum et probatio mentalis devotionis. Status autem exterioris hominis instruit nos de humilitate et affectu interioris.
trad_string: The gesture of the body is an argument and a proof of mental devotion. The external state of the human being instructs us of their humility and internal affect.

text_string: 9 Dixit autem et ad quosdam, qui in se confidebant tamquam iusti, et aspernabantur ceteros, parabolam istam: 10 Duo homines ascenderunt in templum ut orarent: unus pharisaeus, et alter publicanus. 11 Pharisaeus stans, haec apud se orabat: Deus, gratias ago tibi, quia non sum sicut ceteri hominum: raptores, iniusti, adulteri, velut etiam hic publicanus; 12 ieiuno bis in sabbato; decimas do omnium quae possideo. 13 Et publicanus a longe stans, nolebat nec oculos ad caelum levare; sed percutiebat pectus suum, dicens: Deus, propitius esto mihi peccatori. 14 Dico vobis, descendit hic iustificatus in domum suam ab illo: quia omnis qui se exaltat, humiliabitur; et qui se humiliat, exaltabitur.
trad_string:
9 And he spoke also this parable to some who trusted in themselves as being righteous, and despised others: 10 Two men went up into the temple to pray: the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. 11 The Pharisee, standing, prayed thus with himself:
“God, I give thee thanks that I am not as the rest of men: extortioners, unjust, adulterers; as also is this publican. 12 I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of all that I possess.” 13 And the publican, standing afar off, would not so much as lift up his eyes towards heaven; but struck his breast, saying:“God, be merciful to me a sinner.” 14 I say to you: this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

text_string: Si, cum hominibus potentibus volumus aliqua suggerere, son praesuminus nisi cum humilitate et reverentia, quanto magis domino deo universorum cum omni humilitate et puritatis devotione supplicandum est. Et non in multiloquio, sed in puritate cordis et conpunctione lacrimarum nos exaudiri sciamus. Et ideo brevis debet esse et pura oratio, nisi forte ex affectu inspirationis divinae gratiae protendatur. In conventu tamen omnino brevietur oratio, et facto signo a priore pariter surgant.
trad_string: If, when we wish to make some request to powerful people, we dare not do so except with humility and reverence, how much more must we make supplication to the Lord God of all things with all humility and devotion of purity. And we should know that it is not by much speaking but by purity of heart and compunction of tears that we are heard. And therefore, prayer ought to be short and pure, unless perhaps it is prolonged out of the affection by divine grace. In the convent, however, prayer should always be brief, and at the signal from the prior they should rise together.

source_label: Ps.-Hugo de Sancto Victore, Ps.-Bernardus Claraevallensis, Tractatus de statu virtutum
text_string: Christus igitur cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse se aequalem Deo, sed semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens.
trad_string: Christ, since he was in the form of God, did not con sider it robbery to be equal to God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant.

text_string: Nihil ergo aliud est oratio quam mentis deuotio, id est, conuersio in Deum per pium et humilem affectum, fide, spe et caritate subnixa.
trad_string: Therefore, prayer is nothing else than devotion of the mind, that is: a conversion towards God through a pious and humble affect; belief, hope and love attached.

source_label: Humbertus Romanis, Expositio Magistri Humberti super constitutiones fratrum praedicatorum
text_string: Illud autem sciendum est quod genuflexio cum elevatione capitis et oculorum, junctis manibus, dispositio est inter omnes aptior ad orandum, sicut noverunt experti. Genuflexio enim habet humilitatem, elevationem vero capitis et oculorum sequitur facile elevatio cordis, quia anima propter colligationem quam habet cum corpore, facile sequitur dispositiones ejus; manuum vero junctio expressio est affectus. Nihil autem est utilius in oratione quam humilitas, intentio et affectus.
trad_string: There is to know kneeling with the head and eyes raised, and with the hands joined, is among all postures the most suitable for praying, as those with experience know. For kneeling expresses humility; and the raising of the head and the eyes is easily followed by the raising of the heart, because the soul, on account of its connection with the body, easily follows the body's dispositions. The joining of the hands, moreover, is an expression of affection. Now nothing is more useful in prayer than humility, attentiveness, and heartfelt devotion.

text_string: Quisquis enim ita humilatur ut genua figat, adhuc habet quo humiletur; quisquis autem sic humilatur et haereat in terra venter eius, ultra quo humiletur non habet. Si enim ultra voluerit, iam non erit humilare, sed obruere.
trad_string: For whoever humbles himself in such a way as to bend the knee still has room to humble himself further; but whoever humbles himself so deeply that his belly clings to the ground has no further place to humble himself. For if he wanted to go further, it would no longer be humbling, but destroying.

text_string: Ideo sequitur humilitas: et procidit in faciem suam, unde exemplum humilitatis ostendit. Et primo propter humilitatem communem, quia humilitas necessaria est ad orationem (Eccli 35,21: “Oratio humiliantis se nubes penetrabit”).
trad_string: Therefore humility follows: and he fell upon his face, whence he showed an example of humility. And first, on account of the common (general) humility, because humility is necessary for prayer (Sirach 35:21: ‘The prayer of one who humbles himself will pierce the clouds’).

text_string: Aliquando enim orans formam assumit servi, Dominum et iudicem suum humiliter et timorate ad misericordiam provocando, sicut publicanus ille, qui nec oculos audebat ad caelum levare, sed percutiens pectus suum, dicebat: Deus, propitius esto mihi peccatori.
trad_string: Sometimes, indeed, the one praying takes on the form of a servant, humbly and fearfully appealing to his Lord and Judge for mercy, like that publican who did not dare to lift his eyes to heaven, but struck his breast, saying: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

text_string: Est autem oratio dei benivolentie captatio. Item Cassiodorus: Est autem oratio oris ratio, frequens deprecatio et assidua supplicatio, que ab imo pectoris archano procedit cum pietate et devotione. Effectus vero orationis est domini misericordem et propitium nobis efficere.
trad_string: Prayer is to seize the goodwill of God. Cassidorus adds: Prayer is oral reasoning, frequent deprecation and constant supplication, which proceeds from the depths of the heart with piety and devotion. The effect of prayer is to make the Lord merciful and favorable to us.

text_string: Est igitur humilitas sic descripta imitanda, primo quia sue angustie est paciens tolleratrix; ut matrona a viro suo iniuriose tractata pacienter sustinet ne virum dignum vituperio reddat, et si forte vituperio ex verberis lesio foris appareat, illam caute dissimulat asserens se aliunde tale malum incurrisse. Ecclesiastici 2 dicitur: "Aurum et argentum in igne probantur," etc. Unde Augustinus: "Beati, inquit, humiles qui, etsi quando fieri solet ut iniustas audiant increpaciones, amplius se Christo humilient et minus se audire quam meruerunt proclamant."
trad_string: Humility as thus defined must be practiced, first because it patiently endures its troubles; just as a wife who is mistreated by her husband suffers it patiently so that she may not cause her husband to become worthy of public shame, and if perhaps, to his shame, some external lesion from his beating can be seen on her, she carefully dissimulates saying she took an injury elsewhere. In Ecclesiasticus 2 it is said: "Gold and silver are tried in the fire," and so forth. Whence Augustine says: "Blessed are the humble who, if it sometimes happens that they hear unjust accusations against them, humble themselves further before Christ and declare the hear less than they have deserved."

text_string: Secundo, quia mala sua recogitans est bonorum morum occultatrix, sicut pavo aspiciens pedes turpissimos caudam suam dimittit lucentem. Luce 18: "Publicanus a longe stans noluit levare oculos ad celum set percuciens pectus suum ait: 'Deus, propicius,'" etc. Et sequitur: "Amen dico vobis, descendit hic iustificatus in domum suam, quia omnis quis se exaltat, humiliabitur, " etc.
trad_string: Humility must be striven for secondly because it reflects on its shortcomings and hides its good qualities, like the peacock which, seeing that its feet are most vile, forgets about its splendid tail. Therefore in Luke 18: "The Publican, standing afar off, would not lift his eyes up to heaven but striking his breast said: 'Lord, have mercy on me,'" etc. And then follows: "Amen, I say to you, this man went down into his house justified, because everyone that exalts himself will be humbled," etc.

text_string: Tertio, quia operum Christi crebra inspectrix et assecutrix. Ad modum quo aquila contra solem irreverberatis oculis respicit, sic vere humilis opera Christi qui est sol iusticie, Ysaie 66: Ad quem aspiciamus nisi ad humilem", scilicet Christum, ut eum imitemur, scilicet quomodo se Patri humiliavit - cui erat equalis in deitate - in assumpcione humane nature; Philippensium 2: "Qui cum in forma Dei esset", etc. Quomodo se eciam humiliavit parentibus in voluntaria subiectione; Luce 2: "Erat subditus illis." Et tertio erat humilis peccatoribus, quia "usque ad mortem", ut sic sibi humiliemus animas nostras, pro peccatis primo corde conterendo, secundo ore confitendo, et tercio opere satisfaciendo. Et de ists quere in titulo "De confessione".
trad_string: Third, humility must be striven for because it frequently meditates on and follows Christ's deeds. As the eagle looks at the sun with unblinking eyes, just so does a truly humble person look at Christ's deeds, who is the sun of justice. Isaiah 66: "To whom shall we look if not the humble one," that is, Christ, that we may follow him, that is, in the way he has humbled himself before the Father - whose equal he was in divinity -by assuming human nature; Philippians 2: "Who, while he was in the form of God," etc. Further, in the way he humbled himself before his parents in voluntary submission; Luke 2: "He became subject to them." And in the third place he humbled himself before sinners "even unto death," so that we might humble our souls before him, first by having contrition of heart for our sins, second by confession of mouth, and third by satisfaction in deed. On these matters see under the title "On Confession".

source_label: Hugo de Sancto Victore, De quinque septenis
text_string: Deinde quarto loco succedunt septem virtutes. Prima, paupertas spiritus, id est humilitas; secunda, mansuetudo sive benignitas; tertia, compunctio sive dolor; quarta, esuries iustitiae sive desiderium bonum; quinta, misericordia; sexta, cordis munditia; septima, pax.
trad_string: Then, in fourth place, come the seven virtues. First, poverty of spirit, that is, humility; second, meekness or kindness; third, compunction or sorrow; fourth, hunger for righteousness or a good desire; fifth, mercy; sixth, purity of heart; seventh, peace.

source_label: Hugo de Sancto Victore, Duobus modis humilitatem impugnari
text_string: Duobus modis diabolus humilitatem in nobis oppugnat, per iniuriam videlicet, et per reverentiam. Aliquando enim instigat homines, ut iniuriam nobis inferant; ac per hoc ad indignationem, et ad iram, et ad impatientiam nos pertrahere nititur. Aliquando facit illos nobis reverentiam exhibere, et sic ad vanam gloriam, et inanem laetitiam nos inclinare conatur.
trad_string: The devil attacks humility in us in two ways, namely through insult and through reverence. For sometimes he incites people to inflict injury upon us, and through this he strives to drag us toward indignation, anger, and impatience. Other times he causes them to show us reverence, and in this way he attempts to incline us toward vainglory and empty joy.

source_label: Hugo de Sancto Victore, Duobus modis humilitatem impugnari
text_string: Nos vero si contra haec bella inimici humilitatem nostram illaesam custodire volumus, mala nostra iugiter ante oculos habere studeamus. Mala autem dico non solum interiora, quae ad iniquitatem et culpam pertinent, sed etiam exteriora, quae pertinent ad utilitatem: sicut est ignobilitas generis, inopia, quae est mater paupertatis; debilitas corporis, et si qua sunt talia quae hominem humiliant. Nam si culpas nostras et miserias nostras bene et attente inspicere volumus, tunc fortassis nec indignum iudicabimus, si nobis inferatur iniuria; nec dignum, si reverentia exhibeatur.
trad_string: But if we truly wish to keep our humility unharmed against these battles of the enemy, let us strive to keep our own faults constantly before our eyes. By faults, however, I mean not only the interior ones, which pertain to iniquity and sin, but also the exterior ones, which pertain to our benefit: such as lowliness of birth, poverty — which is the mother of want — weakness of body, and whatever else of this kind humbles a person. For if we are willing to look well and attentively upon our sins and our miseries, then perhaps we will judge it neither undeserved, if an injury is inflicted upon us, nor deserved, if reverence is shown.

text_string: Humilitas autem habitus non superabundans in sumptibus et praeparationibus.
trad_string: Humility, moreover, is a disposition that is not excessive in expenditures and preparations.

text_string: Familiares autem ipsius sunt: austeritas, continentia, humilitas, simplicitas, ornatus, bona ordinatio, per se sufficientia.
trad_string: Its companions, moreover, are: austerity, continence, humility, simplicity, refinement, good order, self-sufficiency.

source_label: Richardus de Sancto Victore, De IV gradibus violentae charitatis.
text_string: In hoc itaque statu anime eiusmodi proponitur forma humilitatis Christi, unde et dicitur ei: Hoc sentite in vobis quod et in Christo Ihesu, qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse se equalem Deo, sed semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens, in similitudinem hominum factus, et habitu inventus ut homo; humiliavit autem semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Hec est forma humilitatis Christi ad quam conformare se debet quisquis supremum consummate caritatis gradum attingere volet. Maiorem siquidem caritatem nemo habet quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis.
trad_string: In this state of the soul, therefore, the model of Christ's humility is proposed to it, wherefore it is also said to it: Have this mind in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in appearance as a man; he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. This is the model of Christ's humility to which whoever wishes to attain the highest and perfect degree of charity must conform himself. For no one has greater charity than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

source_label: Richardus de Sancto Victore, De IV gradibus violentae charitatis.
text_string: Ad summum itaque caritatis culmen profecerunt et iam in quarto caritatis gradu positi sunt qui pro amicis animam suam ponere et illud apostolicum implere iam possunt: Estote imitatores Dei sicut filii carissimi, et ambulate in dilectione sicut et Christus dilexit vos et tradidit semetipsum pro vobis oblationem et hostiam Deo in odorem suavitatis. In tertio itaque gradu anima in Deum glorificatur, in quarto propter Deum humiliatur. In tertio gradu conformatur divine claritati, in quarto vero conformatur christiane humilitati.
trad_string: They have therefore advanced to the supreme summit of charity and are already placed in the fourth degree of charity, those who are already able to lay down their lives for their friends and to fulfil that word of the Apostle: Be imitators of God as most beloved children, and walk in love as Christ also loved you and gave himself up for you as an offering and a sacrifice to God as a fragrant aroma. In the third degree, therefore, the soul is glorified in God; in the fourth it is humbled for God. In the third degree it is conformed to the divine glory; in the fourth, however, it is conformed to Christian humility.

text_string: “Caritatem habete, humilitatem servate, pauperitatem voluntariam possidete.” “Habend götliche minn, behalten demütikeit, besitzent willige armüt.”
trad_string: "Have charity, preserve humility, posess voluntary poverty." "Have divine love, preserve humility, posess voluntary poverty."

source_label: Conradus Hirsaugiensis, Dialogus de mundi contemptu vel amore
text_string: Igitur humilitas regina virtutum est, mors viciorum; instrumentum iusticie, nutrix sedula discipline; sanctimonie vigor, sancte religionis rigor; sensati cordis indicium, spiritus sancti testimonium; morum vigilantia, proprie mensure intelligentia; custodia fida virtutum, divine caritatis hospicium; insimulatus affectus, ordo religionis, libertas in periculis, modus in verbis; profectuum magistra, per exemplum doctrix tacita; magnorum contemptus, honeste vite appetitus.
trad_string: Therefore humility is the queen of the virtues, the death of vices; the instrument of justice, the diligent nurse of discipline; the strength of holiness, the discipline of holy religion; the sign of a wise heart, the testimony of the Holy Spirit; watchfulness over conduct, the knowledge of one's own measure; the faithful guardian of the virtues, the dwelling-place of divine charity; unfeigned affection, the ordering of religious life, freedom amid dangers, restraint in speech; the mistress of spiritual progress, a silent teacher through example; contempt for great things, the desire for an upright life.

source_label: Conradus Hirsaugiensis, Dialogus de mundi contemptu vel amore
text_string: Humilis mens doctrine sacre legis intendit, actus suos eque moderatur; nimia fastidit, modum studiis suis ponit; deuote mentis conceptum aperit; ad discendum auida, suauis in doctrina; in faciendo iuditio timida, in arguendo difficilis, ad ignoscendum facilis; immobilis in aduersis, in prosperis eadem; in iniuriis secura, de pace sollicita; in amiciciis cauta, in officiis sedula; quietis amica, magnorum magna contemptrix, in prelatione uerecunda, magis seruire quam imperare parata.
trad_string: The humble mind attends to the teaching of the sacred law and governs its own actions with equity; it recoils from excess, and sets a measure to its studies; it opens up what a devout mind conceives; eager to learn, it is gentle in teaching; timid in passing judgment, reluctant to reproach, ready to forgive; unmoved in adversity, and the same in prosperity; untroubled under injuries, anxious for peace; cautious in friendships, diligent in its duties; a friend of quiet, a great despiser of great things, modest when placed in authority, more ready to serve than to command

source_label: Conradus Hirsaugiensis, Dialogus de mundi contemptu vel amore
text_string: Inest humili habitus equalis, firmus incessus, unitus granis, stabilitas ad eadem, status idem, capax prudentie spiritus, spei gaudium, lasciuie petulantis odium, decor in uirtute, confidentia in terrore, de profectu semper in alta gratiarum actio et de propriis meritis nulla umquam presumptio.
trad_string: In the humble person there is an even bearing, a steady gait, a grave countenance, constancy in the same things, an unchanging state, a spirit capable of prudence, the joy of hope, hatred of wanton frivolity, grace in virtue, confidence in the midst of terror, thanksgiving always directed on high for any progress, and never any presumption about one's own merits.

text_string: Si trüg alwegen gnüg snödes und verworffennes gewand, und umb die behütung der demütikeit, in der si vil fúr traff, so wolt si nit tages uff legen nüwe wil und wisz geweschene sleyger, sunder si trüg si ze nacht ze metti, uncz si gealteten und gebrúnt wurden.
trad_string: She always wore sufficiently shabby and worn-out clothing, and in order to protect the virtue of humility, at which she greatly excelled, similarily she did not want to put on newly white and freshly washed veils during the day. Instead, she wore them tot he nightly mass service until they had become old and browned.

text_string: Doch wolt si lieber ston in der sicherheit der demütikeit, und alle die volkomenen swestren sacztz si ir selbz zü einem exempel und fleisz sich, ir tugenden sich zü verwunderen und ir verdienen grosz und hoch zü scheczen, aber von ir selben nideren ding ze halten, und in ansechen der andren swestren scheczet si ir leben nit eines ögenblickes wert.
trad_string: Yet she preferred to remain within the safety of humility, and she set all the truly perfect sisters before herself as an example. She strove to admire their virtues and to esteem their merits as great and lofty, but to regard herself as lowly; and in comparison with the other sisters she considered her own life not worth even a single moment.

text_string: O, wölte got, daz wir tregen und hinlessigen in unseren versümnissen und súnden hetten die demütikeit, die die helgen swestren do hand gehept in iren tugenden und güten wercken!
trad_string: O, God granted that we, in our shortcomings and sins, possessed the humility that the holy sisters then upheld in their virtues and good works!

text_string: Vil andre tröstung tet ir got der herr in verborgenheit, aber wenn si gar vast schemig und demütig waz, do wolt si si nit offenbaren.
trad_string: God the Lord granted her many other forms of consolation in secrecy, but because she was very coy and deeply humble, she did not want to reveal them.

text_string: Si waz so grosser senftmütikeit und gedult und demütikeit, da wir si nie hand gesechen erczúrnt, noch si nie hand gehört murmlen oder reden wort des zornes.
trad_string: She was of such great gentleness, patience, and humility, that we have never seen her mad nor have we ever heard her murmur or say a word of wrath.

text_string: Si hat ire geng uff geseczt in die füssstapfen unsers herren Jhesu Christi und ist nit hinder sich gangen noch usz getretten uncz si den löff ires weges volbrocht hat, nochvolgende siner demütikeit, siner gedult, siner minn, und den andren tugenden, die er mit worten und mit exemplen het gelert.
trad_string: She set her steps upon the footsteps of out Lord Jesus Christ and did not turn back nor step aside until she had completed the course of her path, following his humility, his patience, his love and the other virtues that he had taught by words and by example.

text_string: Ir tieffi wore demütikeit erhöchet si alwegen vor miner angesicht.
trad_string: Her deep and true humility always exalts her before my sight.

text_string: Und do die swestren, den si söliches seit, sich verwundreten und sprochen si selig um ir grosse luterkeit, zü hand kert si ir selben zü dem verdienen der demütikeit, die so úbertreffenliche gob der götlichen gob und sprach: “Ir söllend wissen in der worheit, daz es nit kunt usz tugend miner kúscheit, daz ich nit kan von unluteren dingen gedenken, sunder es ist ein torheit mines gemütes.”
trad_string: And when the sisters to whom she said this were astonishing and spoke of her blessedness because of her great purity, she immediately turned herself back to the earning of humility, which so surpassingly gives glory to the divine gift of grace, and said: “You should know in truth that it does not come from the virtue of chastity, that I am unable to think of impure things; rather, it is the folly of my mind.

text_string: Die gieng durch den weg der demütikeit und der gehorsam on clag, und si wandlet under den swestren als ein senftmütiges lempli.
trad_string: She went the way of humility and obedience without complaint, and she moved among the sisters like a gentle lamb.

text_string: Do si in daz closter waz ingangen, do fleisz si sich unserem herren zü dienen mit lutrem herczen in demütikeit und in senftmütikeit, und waz in allen dingen sich selben versmochen und verwerffen, so vil volkomenlicher so vil leben in der welt me zart waz gesin in wollústen. Alle tag wüsch si mit iren eignen henden die schússlen und andre geschirr der kuchi mit den dirnen, und half inen öch empcziklich in andren dingen, die do ze tün woren, in denen si inen mocht gehelfen. In disen wercken und den glich hat si lust als in allen richtümen.
trad_string: When she had entered the convent, she devoted herself to serving our Lord with a pure heart, in humility and in gentleness, and in all things she so thoroughly despises and casts herself aside, in proportion as her life in the world had previously been the more delicate in its pleasures. Each day she washed bowls and other kitchen vessels with her own hands together with the serving girls, and she also zealously helped them in other tasks that were required, wherever she was able to assist them. In these works and the like she took as much delight as in all riches.

text_string: Si waz gewurczlet in so grosser senftmütikeit, daz alle ire wort und werck wider luchten mit den zeichen der demütikeit.
trad_string: She was rooted in such great gentleness that all her words and deeds, in return, shone forth with the marks of humility.

text_string: „Ich, do ich grosz und hoch waz in dem höchsten, do bin ich um dinen willen klein und demütig worden uff dem ertrich.“
trad_string: "I who was great and exalted in the highest realm, became, for your sake, small and humble upon the earth."

text_string: In sölichen diensten der miltikeit und der demüttikeit hat si lust, und floch die spil der kinden und ander úppikeit und untugen, mit dem söliche jugent gewonlich bekúmeret ist, waz si flissiklich vermiden.
trad_string: She took delight in such services of kindness and humility, and she avoided the games of the children and other frivolity and misconduct with which such youth is usually burdened with, which she diligently shunned.

text_string: Den dient si emtziklich mit milter sorg und mit unverdrossenem fliss, und nit allein dient si in emptziklichen, me öch die unsuferkeit und die geswer der siechen handlet si mit iren eigenen henden so demüttiklich, so wirdiklichen und so getrúwlichen, als ob si berürt die helgen wunden Christi.
trad_string: She serves them with tireless dedication, with gentle care and unwearied diligence; and not only does she serve them in this constancy, but she also handles the filth and the sores of the sick with her own hands, so humbly, so worthily, and so faithfully, as if she were touching the holy wounds of Christ.

text_string: Aber under andren tugenden ires gemüttes hand wir an ir gesechen ein zü verwundrende gnod der demüttikeit und der gehorssam, also daz si nie mit einem einigen wort sich unwillig bewiset zü gehorssame, sunder on alles widersprechen gehorssamet si dem willen der gebiettenden oder heissenden in allen dingen.
trad_string: But among other virtues of her disposition we have observed in her a grace of humility and obedience worthy of admiration, so that she never show herself unwilling to obey with a single word; rather, without contradiction, she obeyed the will of those who command or instruct her in all things.

text_string: Und die keisserliche jungfrow, die mütter unsers herren, unzüglichlichen schinende von antlit und von gewand mit irem sunderlichen botschaft werber, dem heilgen ertzengel Gabriel, giengen aller erwirdiklichest hin fúr zü dem altar, und zü der rechten sitten des altars böigten si demüttiklich ire heilgen knú.
trad_string: And the imperial virgin, the mother of our Lord, shining without blemish in countenance and in garment, together with her particular messenger and herald, the holy archangel Gabriel, proceeded forward toward the altar with the greatest reverence; and on the right side of the altar they humbly bent their holy knees.

text_string: Ein durlúchtiger groff von Hasburg genant Götfridus, der sasz etwen an dem redfenster der swestren, und die vor geseite swester wa och do, und der groff befal sich demüttiklich und ernstlich in ir gebet.
trad_string: A most illustrious count of Habsburg, called Gottfried, was occasionally sitting at the sister’s speaking window, and the aforesaid sister was also present there. The count commended himself humbly and earnestly to her prayers.

text_string: Doch so lucht offenbarlichen in ir gantze gehorssam und grosse demüttikeit. Wann in allen iren tagen ires lebens hat si me denn in allen richtum lust in den wercken der demüttikeit und der verworffenheit.
trad_string: In her complete obedience and great humility shines forth openly. For throughout all the days of her life she took more delight than all riches in the works of humility and abasement.

text_string: Sy waz der grösten demüttikeit und gehorssam, und waz alwegen milt und erbarmhertzig, wann durch die meisterschaft der götlichen gnoden hat si gelert milt und demuttig ze sin von hertzen.
trad_string: She was of the greatest humility and obedience and was always gentle and merciful; for throughout the discipline of divine grace she had learned to be gentle and humble from the heart.

text_string: Do dient si unsrem herren ernstlich untz in iren tod, in grosser demüttikeit und senftmüttikeit.
trad_string: Thus she served the Lord earnestly until her death, in great humility and gentleness.

text_string: Welher mensch aber sich selber ausser göttlicher minne vnd lieb mit eim reinen lautern hertzen vnd mit einr guten gewissen vnd mit eim waren, vesten, vngestifften glauben in allen dingen lat vnd sich got gentzlich gibt vnd bevihlt in lieb vnd in layd vnd mit slehten worten in allem leiden vnd widerwertikeit vnd betrübnüß vnd dem gotlichen willen demütiklich mit williger gedult vnd gelassenheit, dankberlich gehorsam ist, sig, diz ist rehter, warer, sicher vnd gewisser andaht vnd ist auch ie vnd ie gut vnd gereht vnd von got all zeit vnd nit von der natur noch von dem bösen geist vnd ist auch ein sicher gewisse zeichen rehter warer heilikeit vnd rechtes andahtes.
trad_string: But whoever lets himself go in everything out of godly love with a pure and clear heart, and with a good consciousness and with a true, strong, unfaked faith, and who gives oneself to God completely in love and pain; and whoever is thankfully obedient with plain words in all pain and hardship and sadness, [whoever is thankfully obedient] to gods will, humbly, with chosen patience and reliance, look: this is the right, true, safe and certain kind of devotion, and it is also good and just, always from God, never from nature or the evil spirit, and it is furthermore a safe and certain sign of right, true holiness and right devotion.

text_string: Die erste pforte an disen uͤbungen das ist ein tieffe verworffene demuͤtekeit, daz der mensche von ime selber zuͦmole nút enthalte und kúnne sich in lidender wisen gedrucken under Got und alle creaturen unde ein ieglich ding wo es herkome, das er daz demuͤtecliche von Gotte neme und von nieman anders, und las sich Gotte in einer demuͤtigen vorhte, in woreme versmohende sich selber in allen dingen, in liebe und in leide, in habende und in darbende.
trad_string: The first door to these exercises is a deep, cast‑away humility: that a person holds himself to be nothing at all and is able, in a suffering way, to press himself beneath God and all creatures and every thing, wherever it may come from; that he receives it humbly from God and from no one else, and so leaves himself to God in humble fear, in true self‑contempt in all things - in love and in suffering, in having or in want.

text_string: Dis ist ein kunst do alle kúnste inne beslossen sint der man zuͦ warer heilikeit bedarf; daz were ware demuͤtikeit sunder alle glose und nút in den worten oder in dem schine, sunder in der worheit und in dem grunde.
trad_string: This is an art in which all arts are enclosed that one needs for true holiness: namely true humility, without all gloss or pretense, not in words or in outward appearance, but in truth and in the ground.

text_string: Alles daz der mensche moͤhte haben in eigen willen, es si Got oder creature, do ist ime unzellicher vil nútzer ein willig demuͤtig darben desseben und alles habendes in rechter gelossenheit und in uzgon dins willen in gelossenheit.
trad_string: All that a person might want to possess in self‑will, be it God or creature, it is for him incomparably more beneficial to be willingly and humbly deprived of that very thing, and to have all things in right letting-go, in the surrender of your will in letting-go.

text_string: Und alsus so hanget rechte der mensche enzwúschent himmel und erden: mit sinen úbersten kreften so ist er erhaben úber sich selber und úber alle ding und wonet in Gotte, aber mit sinen nidersten kreften so ist er verdunst under alle ding in den grunt der demuͤtekeit und ist rechte also ein anhabende mensche, in der allerniedersten uͤbunge kan er sich halten, do er es zuͤ dem aller ersten begunde, und verkleinet kein ding, wie snoͤde es ouch si, und het in eime ieglichem gewaren frieden; und alsus ist er ein wesenlich gezúg unsers herren, das er der ist der von dem himmel kummen ist nider, wider in den himmel gevarn ist und úber alle himmele.
trad_string: And thus the human being is rightly placed between heaven and earth: with his highest powers he is lifted above himself and above all things and dwells in God; but with his lowest powers he sinks beneath all things into the ground of humility. And thus he is truly a beginner: in the very lowest exercises he can remain there where he first began, and he despises no thing, however base it may be, and in every single thing he has true peace. And thus he is an essential witness of our Lord, that he is the one who came down from heaven, ascended again into heaven, and is above all heavens.

text_string: Daz dis gemuͤte ge mit minnen in, in inniger begerunge, in einem demuͤtigen underwurffe under Got, das ist dis wore gebet alleine.
trad_string: That the soul should enter with love, with outmost desire, humbly submitting to God - this alone is true prayer.

text_string: Got suͦcht und wil haben einen demuͤtigen menschen, einen senftmuͤtigen menschen, einen armen menschen, einen lutern menschen und einen gelossenen menschen der gelich ste.
trad_string: God is searching for and wants to have a humble person, a gentle-minded person, a poor person, a pure person, and a let-go person who perseveres in equanimity.

text_string: Do noch bat si demüttiklichen und ernstlichen, daz si in daz closter enpfangen wurd zü dem dienst der kuchi als lang si lebt.
trad_string: After that, she humbly and earnestly requested she be accepted into the convent for service in the kitchen as long as she lived.

text_string: Doch welt si lieber demüttig und verworffen sin in diser zit, daz si in den himlen mit dester grösserer er wurde schinen vor unsrem herren. Also dient si in der kuchi und in andren diensten der swestren demüttiklich alle ir tag, und si kam zü grosser heilikeit und volkomenheit des lebens mit hilff der gnoden gottes.
trad_string: Yet, she preffered to be humble and despised in this life, so that she might shine before our Lord in heaven all the more greatly. Thus she served in the kitchen and in other services for the sisters, humbly throughout all her days, and through God's grace she attained great holiness and perfection of life.

text_string: Si sind von unsrem herren fúrkomen in dem segnen der süssikeit, wele götlichen himelsche süssikeit hie in diser zit ervolget wirt mit reinikeit des inneren und des usseren mönschen, mit senftmüttiger demüttikeit des hertzen und der usseren wandlung, mit andechtiger volbringung des götlichen dienstes, mit flissiger nochfolgung oder behaltung des ordens und der gehorsam in lutterer ungestifteter götlicher minn.
trad_string: They have been brought forth by our Lord in the blessings of sweetness, a divine heavenly sweetness that is attained in this life thorugh purity of the inner and outer person, through gentle humility of the heart and outward conduct, through devout performance of divine service, through diligent observance and preservation of the order and of obedience, in pure undivided divine love.

text_string: “Caritatem habete, humilitatem servate, pauperitatem voluntariam possidete.” “Habend götliche minn, behalten demütikeit, besitzent willige armüt.”
trad_string: "Have charity, preserve humility, posess voluntary poverty." "Have divine love, preserve humility, posess voluntary poverty."

text_string: Die brüder und die vorgeseite swester Gertrut stünden erwirdiklich uf gegen ir und mit demüttikeit seitten si ir, daz si umb herberg dar weren komen zü der stund.
trad_string: The brothers and the aforementioned Sister Getrut stood up venerably before her, and with humbly told her that they had come there at that time to search for hospitality.

text_string: Si stünd snelliklichen uf und sasz bald uf irem wagen, und si und der provincial mit sinen gesellen seitten der selben frowen demüttiklich grosse gnod und danck umb die grossen und manigfaltigen güttet, die si inen hat bewiset, und gesegneten si demüttiklich und schieden enweg.
trad_string: She rose promptlyand soon took her seat on her wagon. She and the provincial, together with his companions, expressed to that woman humble and heartfelt gratitude and thanks for the great manifold kindness she had shown them. They humbly bestowed their blessings upon her and then departed.

text_string: Do antwirtet si demüttiklich: “Ich mag mit dem leben nit gesechen got minen herren gecrútzget. Wann ich in also ansech so brech mir min hertz.”
trad_string: She answered humbly: "I cannot behold my Lord God crucified and continue to live. For wherever I look at him, my heart breaks within me."

text_string: Also kam diese swester wider und hat usz der mossen einen demüttigen wandel. Si hat ir selben an ein zedel geschriben alle ir liplichen und geistlichen gebresten, die lasz si dick ir selben zü demüttigung.
trad_string: Thus the sister retunred and thereafter lived a life of extraordinary humility. She wrote down for herself on a slip of paper all her bodily and spiritual shortcomings, and she often read it for her own humbling.

text_string: Öch von grosser demüttikeit müttet si nieman an keinen dienst fúr si ze tünd, wele ir aber út dienstes ted, der kond si gnüg demüttiklich gedancken. Si fleisz sich alwegen ze haben die unwegesten becher, messer, löffel, schússlen und des glich und daz verbrant eschecht brot, die gebrochenen usz gelöffenen eyger, und daz minst angericht.
trad_string: Also out of great humility, she never compelled anyone to perform any service for her. But if someone did offer her their services, she would thank that person very humbly. She always strove to take the poorest cups, knives, spoons, bowls, and the like, as well as burnt and stale bread, cracked and emptied eggshells, and the least desirable dishes.

text_string: Aber denn ligen die schefflin Christi in dem grünen grasz, so si durch demüttikeit sich neigen oder ire knú böigen oder nider fallen uf ire antlit vor dem bild der wirdigen mütter gottes und der lieben heilgen, und si anrüffen zü fúrbittern und zü fúr sprechen vor got irem sun unsrem herren.
trad_string: But then Christ's little sheep lie down in the green grass when, through humility, they bow themselves, bend their knees, or fall down upon their faces before the image of worthy Mother of God and the beloved saints, invoking them to plead and to speak on their behalf before God, her Son, our Lord.

text_string: Der selb milt got des ewigen gottes sun unser herr Jhesus Christus, der durch die predige sins userwelten fúrlöiffers und sins aller wirdigesten töiffers sancti Johannis baptiste und durch daz exempel sins aller strengesten heilgesten lebens het vor gekúndet und erzöiget, und in den tagen siner demüttikeit selber het geheilget daz sacrament der volkomenen penitentz und selber geleit daz fundament der woren geistlicheit [...]
trad_string: The same gracious God, the Son of the eternal God, our Lord Jesus Christ, who through the preaching of his chosen forerunner and most worthy baptizer, Saint John the Baptist, and through the example of his most strictly religious and holy life, had proclaimed and demonstrated this; and who, in the days of his humility, himself sanctified the sacrament of perfect penance himself laid the foundation of true spirituality [...]

text_string: Der selb herr unser got durch die verdienen und fúrbitten unser heilgen mütteren, von der leben und sitten wir etwaz geschriben hand zü bessrung der noch komenden, geb uns iren füsz stapffen also an ze halten, denn sinn ir demüttikeit und einfaltikeit also ze halten, daz wir durch daz mit wúrcken siner gnoden verdienen ze komen zü der ere der ewigen selikeit, zü der wir on zwiffel glöben daz die selben unser heilgen mütteren komen sigen, amen.
trad_string: May the same Lord our God, through the merits and intercessions of our holy mothers, concerning whose lives and conduct we have written something for the edification of posterity, grant that we may follow in their footsteps; that is, emulate their humility and simplicity, so that through this, by the working of his grace, we may merit to attain the glory of eternal blessedness, to which, without doubt, we believe these same holy mothers have achieved. Amen.

text_string: Der erwirdigen geistlichen dienerin Christi, swester Elisabet, priorin des closters sancti Johannis baptiste in Underlinden prediger ordens, wunschet der demüttig brüder des selben ordens, brüder Johannes, fúr ein grüsz den ursprung und den wúrcker unsers heiles Christum Jhesum ze tragen im hertzen und mit kreften, begeren, und flissen noch ze folgen sinen füsz stapffen úwer götlichen minn.
trad_string: To Christ’s venerable spiritual servant, sister Elisabet, prioress of the convent St. John the Baptist at Unterlinden of the Order of the Preachers, Brother Johannes, a humble member of the same order, sends greetings, wishing that she may bear in her heart and with all her strength Jesus Christ, the source and author of our salvation, and that through divine love she may desire and diligently endeavor to follow in his footsteps.

text_string: Do viel si demüttiklich an ir venye uf daz ertrich, und von der zit ward si aller volkomenlichest gesund.
trad_string: Then she humbly fell in venia to the ground and was thereafter fully healed.

text_string: Din gewand sig haben demüttikeit in der gestalt, hertikeit in dem anrüren, armüt in dem gelt oder kosten.
trad_string: Your clothing should exhibit humility in appearance, roughness to the touch, and poverty in its price or cost.

text_string: Aber dis soltu wissen vor allen dingen, daz alle die vorgeseiten ding dir nit nútz weren, es sy denn daz du mit der gesegneten jungfrowen Maria besitzest die aller tieffeste demüttikeit.
trad_string: But above all things you shall know, that all the aforementioned things will be of no use to you unless you possess, together with the blessed Virgin Mary, the deepest humility of all.

text_string: Dis ist die forcht die usz demüttikeit kunt und sachet öch die demüttikeit, die allein enttrint den stricken des bösen geistes, als dem heilgen sant Anthonio geoffenbart wart.
trad_string: This is the fear that arises from humility and in turn gives rise to humility, which alone disentangled itself from the snares of the evil spirit, as was revealed to the holy Saint Anthony.

text_string: Du sigest gegen in allen demüttig und güttig, und in den dingen, die du hest inen uf ze legen, soltu gebruchen bittung und manung me denn gewalt des gebietten.
trad_string: Be humble and kind toward them all, and in those matters that you have to impose upon them, you should make rather use petition and exhortation than the power of command.
